chief_complaint: Localized swelling on her left leg.
history_of_present_illness: The swelling developed slowly over the past 3 weeks, is itchy but not painful, with no history of fever or arthropod bites.
exposure_and_epidemiology: She just returned from a 6-week backpacking trip to Ghana.
physical_exam: There is localized swelling on the left leg, about 1.5cm in diameter, with slightly hyperaemic surrounding skin, a blackish scab, and no lymphadenopathy; the rest of the physical examination is normal.
differential_diagnosis: Rickettsial disease, cutaneous anthrax, spider bites, localized bacterial skin and soft-tissue infections (folliculitides, furuncles, carbuncles, or abscesses), and infestation with fly maggots (myiasis).
management_and_clinical_course: The scab was removed, revealing pulsating and oozing transparent fluid; the lesion was covered with white petroleum jelly and bandaged, and two days later, the maggot of a Tumbu fly was easily removed with forceps, resulting in a clean lesion requiring no further treatment.
final_diagnosis: Cutaneous furuncular myiasis caused by Tumbu fly larvae (Cordylobia anthropophaga).
